# Free third-party material

Code and files from other projects that are free software, the kind Debian main takes. XeStrata may build and run
with them. Each project's folder keeps its own license text.

| Folder | Project | License | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ggml/` | [ggml / llama.cpp](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp) | MIT (`ggml/LICENSE`) | `ggml-common.h`, an unmodified copy at the commit in `ggml/VERSION.txt` (it stays MIT): the block layouts and codebook grids of the quantized formats. `ggml-common-tq.h`, from upstream Strata's copy of Agention's llama.cpp fork (agentionai/llama.cpp 073bc9e68, MIT): the trellis formats of the Gyro files (TQ2_T, TQK6, TQK7) and their codebook, unchanged; the pair-trellis blocks of the Gyro-Coder files (TQP5, TQP6, TQP7) from the fork's 9aa51ce ([gitlab.com/agentionai-group/llama.cpp](https://gitlab.com/agentionai-group/llama.cpp)), unchanged. Needed to build the engine. Update it only together with the pinned llama.cpp (the engine also links ggml-cpu from it) |
| `intel-llvm/` | [intel/llvm](https://github.com/intel/llvm) (DPC++) | Apache-2.0 with LLVM exceptions (`intel-llvm/LICENSE.TXT`) | Not the compiler itself, which `tools/intel_llvm_build.py` clones from intel/llvm at the release it pins (v7.2.0) and builds into `.tools/`: XeStrata's fixes to it, `patches/NN-<id>.patch`, which the script applies in order before building. They are under intel/llvm's license, as changes to its files; each says what it fixes. The deb and rpm packages carry the SYCL runtime of the intel/llvm built so (`libsycl`, UR's loader and adapters, `libumf`), with this license text |
| `rocm-device-libs/` | [ROCm's device libraries](https://github.com/ROCm/llvm-project/tree/f30ae3e6b680ad23dcf522e668c6d4c5c90838d0/amd/device-libs) (ocml, ockl and the others), by AMD | University of Illinois/NCSA (`rocm-device-libs/LICENSE.TXT`) | Not the libraries themselves, which `tools/intel_llvm_build.py` clones from ROCm's llvm-project at the commit it pins (ROCm 7.14.1's, on the same LLVM as the intel/llvm it builds) and builds with intel/llvm into `.tools/`, with the target features Debian's rocm-llvm package gives their build (transcribed from its `debian/rules`, Expat: see NOTICE); without them CMake takes a ROCm's device libraries the compiler reads (`cmake/StrataHip.cmake`). The AMD code links them: the engine's kernels for AMD GPUs carry parts of them, so the deb and rpm packages carry this license text |
| `oneDNN/` | [oneDNN](https://github.com/uxlfoundation/oneDNN) | Apache-2.0, with the parts other projects' licenses cover (`oneDNN/LICENSE`, `oneDNN/THIRD-PARTY-PROGRAMS`) | Not oneDNN itself, which `CMakeLists.txt` fetches at the tag it pins (`v3.14.2`, its archive's SHA-256 checked), or takes from `STRATA_ONEDNN_SOURCE`, and builds with the engine's compiler for Intel GPUs only (its SYCL GPU runtime) beside the build, with two of oneDNN's pull requests backported to the tag (`oneDNN/patches/`: #6468, the SDPA's fused backward packing its strides once, and #6472, the same backward on xe_hpg, the Arc A series; under oneDNN's license). The attention on Intel GPUs, the image engine's and the plain models' prompt (its SDPA, `src/kernels/xe/sdpa_onednn.cpp`), the VAEs' convolutions and the int8 products. Windows: cross-built as the engine is, without its VTune hooks (`DNNL_ENABLE_JIT_PROFILING`, `DNNL_ENABLE_ITT_TASKS`: their assembly is MASM's), and `dnnl.dll` goes into the 7z. Ubuntu's `libdnnl-sycl` is built for another SYCL runtime than intel/llvm's, so it is not used |
| `cudnn-frontend/` | [cuDNN Frontend](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend) | Apache-2.0, parts MIT (`cudnn-frontend/LICENSE.txt`) | Not the headers themselves, which `CMakeLists.txt` fetches at the tag it pins (`v1.32.2`, its archive's SHA-256 checked) in the contrib-llvm mode where cuDNN's own headers are found: the image engine's attention on NVIDIA GPUs (cuDNN's SDPA, `src/image/qi_sdpa.cpp`), Linux and Windows. cuDNN itself is NVIDIA's and not free software: the engine opens it at run time where the user installed it (`libcudnn.so.9`, `cudnn64_9.dll`), and takes its own kernel without it. Header-only, compiled into the image engine: the contrib-llvm packages and the Windows 7z carry this license text |
| `cutlass/` | [CUTLASS](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cutlass) | BSD-3-Clause (`cutlass/LICENSE.txt`; its `python/CuTeDSL`, which XeStrata does not use, is under NVIDIA's EULA) | Not the headers themselves, which `CMakeLists.txt` fetches at the tag it pins (`v4.8.1`, its archive's SHA-256 checked) in the contrib-llvm mode for NVIDIA GPUs from sm_80 on: the int8 products whose sums leave scaled as BF16 (`src/kernels/cuda/i8_gemm_cutlass.cu`, `kernels::i8_gemm_bf16`), compiled by intel/llvm's clang as CUDA, not by nvcc. Header-only, compiled into the engine: the contrib-llvm packages and the Windows 7z carry this license text |
| `comfy-kitchen/` | [comfy-kitchen](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/comfy-kitchen), by Comfy Org | Apache-2.0, parts derived from SageAttention (Apache-2.0) (`comfy-kitchen/LICENSE`, `comfy-kitchen/NOTICE`) | Not its source, which `CMakeLists.txt` fetches at the tag it pins (`v0.2.41`, its archive's SHA-256 checked) where the build has AMD GPUs with WMMA (RDNA3, RDNA4), in both modes: its HIP int8 product with the scales and bias in its epilogue (`kernels::i8_gemm_bf16`) and its int8 attention (SageAttention's scheme, `kernels::flash_attn_i8`), built by intel/llvm's clang as HIP into a module of its own that the engine opens on an AMD GPU only (`src/kernels/hip/kitchen_module.cpp`), Linux only. XeStrata's patch (`comfy-kitchen/patches/`: the bf16 WMMA builtins' operands as intel/llvm's clang declares them; under comfy-kitchen's license) is applied to it. The deb and rpm packages carry the module, with these texts |
| `aotriton/` | [AOTriton](https://github.com/ROCm/aotriton) | MIT (`aotriton/LICENSE`); its kernels' images can carry parts of AMD's aiter (MIT, `aotriton/LICENSE.aiter`), FlyDSL's kernels (Apache-2.0, `aotriton/LICENSE.FlyDSL`) and Triton (MIT, `aotriton/LICENSE.triton`), which its build compiles them with | Not AOTriton itself, whose release `CMakeLists.txt` fetches (`0.14.2b`: the library built for the build's ROCm and the kernels' images for its AMD architectures, each archive's SHA-256 checked), or takes from `STRATA_AOTRITON_ROOT`: the image engine's attention on AMD GPUs (its flash attention, `src/image/qi_sdpa.cpp`); the text engine does not load it, and the image engine opens it, through a module of its own, on an AMD GPU only. On Windows, where AOTriton has no release, the library is built from the tag's source (its NOIMAGE mode, the images Linux's) with XeStrata's patch (`aotriton/patches/`: HIP's headers and import library given, the build machine's Python; under AOTriton's license) and the 7z carries it, its images and these texts. A ROCm it has no build for takes XeStrata's own kernel. The deb and rpm packages carry its library and images, with these license texts |
| `xz/` | [XZ Utils](https://tukaani.org/xz/) | 0BSD (`xz/COPYING.0BSD`) | Not XZ Utils itself, whose release `CMakeLists.txt` fetches (`5.8.4`, its archive's SHA-256 checked) on Windows: its liblzma, built static and linked into AOTriton's library there. The Windows 7z carries this text |
| `llama.cpp/` | [llama.cpp](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp) | MIT (its own `LICENSE`) | Not in the repository: setup fetches it at the pinned commit. ggml-cpu for the CPU experts and `gguf-py` for the tools. The deb and rpm packages carry `gguf-py` with llama.cpp's `LICENSE` |
| `oneMath/` | [oneMath](https://github.com/uxlfoundation/oneMath) | Apache-2.0 (`oneMath/LICENSE`) | Not oneMath itself, which `CMakeLists.txt` fetches from XeStrata's fork ([MistVVK/oneMath](https://github.com/MistVVK/oneMath), branch `xestrata`) at the tag it pins (`xestrata-13`, its archive's SHA-256 checked), or takes from `STRATA_ONEMATH_SOURCE` (a local archive or URL); in the contrib-llvm mode, and in the free mode for AMD GPUs. The fork is oneMath's commit 6ff3a43 with XeStrata's changes as commits and oneMath's `develop` merged into it (up to 1308c5e), under oneMath's license, each marking the files it changes in their headers: the cuBLAS backend's BF16 product (oneMath has none), the rocBLAS backend's 16-bit products through hipBLASLt where it has kernels for the GPU (ROCm 7.1's rocBLAS has no tuned ones for RDNA4), the int8 products with int32 output in the rocBLAS backend (through hipBLASLt likewise) and the cuBLAS backend (oneMath has them in neither), hipBLASLt's algorithms timed on a large product's first call where a program asks for it (`ONEMATH_HIPBLASLT_TUNE=1`, the image engine), the cuBLAS and rocBLAS backends' SYCL targets on their own libraries, so that one build makes both, and the rocBLAS backend without what HIP and SYCL deprecate (HIP's context API, the comparisons with `HIP_SUCCESS`, `get_access` for a host accessor), and on Windows the compile and link lines and SYCL target of the other platforms for the GNU-style clang++ driver (XeStrata's cross build from Linux), in place of clang-cl's, and the cuBLAS and rocBLAS backends, built there too, with the CUDA and ROCm headers and Windows import libraries the cross build gives, and oneMKL's SYCL link there without `-fsycl-allow-device-image-dependencies`, from oneMKL's own MKLConfig as from the fork's copy (intel/llvm v7.2.0's driver makes it an `/INCLUDE` of a symbol of every library, the MSVC runtime's among them, and a backend's DLL did not link), and the rocBLAS backend's work taken into a SYCL graph being recorded (its native command's HIP stream captured into the graph's HIP graph, as the cuBLAS backend does; before, it ran once at the recording and was left out of the replays). oneMath runs the dense matrix products through its oneMKL (Intel), cuBLAS (NVIDIA) and rocBLAS (AMD) backends. The deb and rpm packages carry the oneMath built so (its rocBLAS backend; the contrib-llvm ones its oneMKL and cuBLAS backends too), and the Windows 7z its oneMKL, cuBLAS and rocBLAS backends, with this license text |
| (none: NuGet) | The launcher's NuGet packages: [Avalonia](https://github.com/AvaloniaUI/Avalonia), [SkiaSharp and HarfBuzzSharp](https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp) (with Skia and HarfBuzz), [FSharp.Core](https://github.com/dotnet/fsharp), [Tmds.DBus.Protocol](https://github.com/tmds/Tmds.DBus), [MicroCom.Runtime](https://github.com/kekekeks/MicroCom), on Windows [ANGLE](https://github.com/AvaloniaUI/angle) (Avalonia's build) | MIT; Skia BSD-3-Clause with the licenses of the parts it carries (FreeType FTL, libpng, zlib, expat, libjpeg-turbo, libwebp, Adobe's DNG SDK, piex Apache-2.0), HarfBuzz MIT, ANGLE BSD-3-Clause | Not in the repository: `dotnet restore` fetches them from nuget.org (`launcher/nuget.config`) at the versions and hashes `launcher/*/packages.lock.json` pin. The launcher's window (`launcher/`) is built of them. The Windows 7z and the `xestrata-gui` deb and rpm carry them, with their license texts and `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` (`tools/package/launcher_notices.py`); of Adobe's DNG SDK in `libSkiaSharp` the code only, none of its documentation, whose terms are not free. The .NET runtime is not carried: Windows' and the distribution's run the window |
| `quantscope/` | [quantscope](https://github.com/1872183316/quantscope) | MIT or Apache-2.0, at your option (`quantscope/LICENSE-MIT`, `quantscope/LICENSE-APACHE`) | `quantscope.py`, unmodified at commit bfdf205 but for a line saying where it comes from (as upstream Strata took it, #911): it reads a GGUF's headers only (a file, a folder, a URL, a ModelScope or Hugging Face repository). `tools/strata_inspect.py` and `setup.py --inspect` use it to say what a GGUF really is and whether XeStrata runs it. Without it only that check is gone |
| `stb/` | [stb](https://github.com/nothings/stb) | MIT or public domain (the Unlicense), at your option (`stb/LICENSE`, the header's own end) | `stb_image.h` v2.30, unmodified (the copy llama.cpp carries in `vendor/stb`): the image engine (`strata-image`) reads an edit's reference image with it (PNG, JPEG, BMP, GIF). Needed to build the image engine |
| `xgrammar/` | [XGrammar](https://github.com/mlc-ai/xgrammar) | Apache-2.0 (`xgrammar/LICENSE`, `xgrammar/NOTICE`) | Not XGrammar itself, which `CMakeLists.txt` fetches at its release v0.2.8 (its archive's SHA-256 checked) and builds from its C++ sources into the engine (`STRATA_GRAMMAR`, on by default): grammar-constrained decoding, the tokens a reply may write next under a JSON schema, a structural tag, a regex or a grammar (`src/core/grammar.cpp`). It carries picojson (`picojson/`). The deb and rpm packages and the Windows 7z carry these license texts |
| `picojson/` | [picojson](https://github.com/kazuho/picojson) | BSD-2-Clause (`picojson/LICENSE`, from its header) | The JSON reader in XGrammar's sources, compiled into the engine with it, and read by `src/core/grammar.cpp` |
| `dlpack/` | [DLPack](https://github.com/dmlc/dlpack) | Apache-2.0 (`dlpack/LICENSE`) | Not DLPack itself, the one header XGrammar's sources read, which `CMakeLists.txt` fetches at commit bbd2f4d (its archive's SHA-256 checked) |
| `aozora-bunko/` | [Aozora Bunko](https://www.aozora.gr.jp/) | Public domain (`aozora-bunko/README.md`, `LICENSES/LicenseRef-PublicDomain.txt`) | Natsume Soseki's novel "Nowaki" (1907) as plain text, its ruby readings dropped (`aozora-bunko/README.md` says how it was made from Aozora Bunko's file and keeps the file's bibliographic notes): the long-context set of `tools/quant_quality.py`, whose token ids `data/quant_quality/long/set.ids.json` holds. Not in the packages |
| `py3langid/` | [py3langid](https://github.com/adbar/py3langid) (a fork of Marco Lui's langid.py) | BSD-3-Clause (`py3langid/LICENSE`) | py3langid 0.4.0's package (`py3langid/py3langid/`: its code and its trained model `data/model.npz.xz`, an LZMA-compressed NumPy archive read without pickle), unchanged, from PyPI's sdist (`py3langid-0.4.0.tar.gz`, SHA-256 `5924159039b5cc282c2edc10a7ea9363b2099834a0e99ed8d5bea3cc435d7871`; `py3langid/PROVENANCE.md` holds each file's). The translation APIs (`serve/translate.py`) detect a source text's language with it (`source_lang` left out, LibreTranslate's `/detect`); it needs NumPy only. Of PLaMo 3 Translate's 53 languages it knows all but Cebuano. The deb and rpm packages and the Windows 7z carry it, with this license text |
| `outfit/` | [Outfit](https://github.com/Outfitio/Outfit-Fonts) | SIL Open Font License 1.1 (`outfit/OFL.txt`) | The web app's font (WOFF2, Latin and Latin Extended). Without it the web app uses the system font |
| `mermaid/` | [mermaid](https://mermaid.js.org/) | MIT, Copyright (c) 2014 - 2022 Knut Sveidqvist (`mermaid/LICENSE`); the script bundles packages under ISC, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, EPL-2.0 (elkjs, of its EPL-2.0 or GPL-3.0-or-later) and MIT, listed with their versions in `mermaid/BUNDLED.md` | mermaid 12.3.0's `dist/mermaid.min.js`, unchanged; `mermaid/PROVENANCE.json` holds the npm tarball's integrity and each file's SHA-256. The web app's chat draws a ```` ```mermaid ```` block as a flowchart with it, once the answer is written (the image tools' plan of steps); the server hands it out at `/web/vendor/mermaid/dist/mermaid.min.js` (`serve/webfiles.py`). Without it the block stays as its source text. The deb and rpm packages and the Windows 7z carry it |
| `katex/` | [KaTeX](https://katex.org/) | MIT, Copyright (c) 2013-2020 Khan Academy and other contributors (`katex/LICENSE`) | KaTeX 0.19.1 (`dist/`: `katex.min.js`, `katex.min.css` and the 20 WOFF2 fonts), as upstream Strata vendors 0.19.0 in `serve/web/vendor/katex` (a965c962c): the package's files unchanged but for `katex.min.css`, whose `@font-face` rules lost their WOFF and TTF fallbacks. `katex/PROVENANCE.json` holds the npm tarball's integrity and each file's SHA-256. The web app's chat draws math with it when Chat settings > Render math is on; the server hands it out at upstream's URL, `/web/vendor/katex/` (`serve/webfiles.py`). Without it the formulas stay as their source text. The deb and rpm packages and the Windows 7z carry it |
| `containers-common/` | [containers/common](https://github.com/containers/container-libs/tree/main/common) (Podman's configuration) | Apache-2.0 (`containers-common/LICENSE`) | `seccomp-io_uring.json`: Podman's seccomp profile, `pkg/seccomp/seccomp.json` at `common/v0.66.0`, with one entry added that allows `io_uring_setup`, `io_uring_enter` and `io_uring_register` (under the project's license, as a change to its file). `container/compose.yaml` runs the container with it: the engine pins its expert arena with io_uring's fixed buffers for an Intel GPU (#42), which Podman's own profile denies. Not in the packages |
